doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Mongo Santamaria and early recording sessions
title: The Swinger from Rio sessions and Lord's discography
summary: Laws recalls flamboyant flute on Sergio Mendes's The Swinger from Rio. Brown shows him Tom Lord's discography with its 333 entries.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Next date is with Sergio Mendes, and Antonio Carlos Jobim is on it.
I remember that. Nesuhi was so impressed. I just did some little flamboyant stuff on the flute that anybody could do, and he’s just flipping. But see, here again, the right

place at the right time, influencing the right people. Yeah, I played on that record. It’s called The Swinger from Rio. Recently they had a party – no, they have a party coming up for him, March 10th. The reason I know that date is because my dad’s birthday was March 10th. It’s interesting. You said April, because you’ve got the dates of those recordings? I didn’t even know that. I don’t have that in mine.
How the heck did you find . . . ?
We can hook you up. When we interviewed Kenny Burrell, I said, “Kenny, you’ve got over 600 titles.” He said, “What?”
Yeah, I don’t know how many I have. I wouldn’t know. You mean, that we played with other people, right?
